correspondence.component_scope: Chosen opening and westward southern reach
correspondence.finding: The opening and westward reach lie in the northern Nogolí vicinity, but the inspected originals do not continuously depict that chosen passage. A nearby Río Nogolí label and Nogolí reservoir are not sufficient to name it or prove a reservoir passage.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern turn and northward approach to the collector
correspondence.finding: The selection turns north west of the Nogolí setting and approaches the southern Vilance drainage. The originals do not establish the entire selected transfer. The provincial study distinguishes southward Nogolí/Bebedero drainage from Vilance and describes engineered interbasin water imports; neither observation identifies this selected line as an aqueduct or natural channel.

The northward lowland corridor west of the Villa General Roca approach corresponds to the collector depicted in the provincial Figure D. IGN shows the same regional drainage with less continuous detail. No separate tributary fragment is selected; lateral mapped feeders are not assigned the collector name.

The northward course follows the labeled Bajo Retamo collector toward Pampa de las Salinas, between the western serranías and the eastern Sierra de San Luis drainage. Both originals distinguish it from neighboring drainage systems.

correspondence.component_scope: Approach to the southern salina margin
correspondence.finding: IGN depicts the named collector entering the southern Pampa de las Salinas setting. The provincial study explains the basin’s northward ephemeral drainage. The regional receiving relationship is supported without asserting perennial flow or a surveyed name boundary.

correspondence.component_scope: Final salina continuation and actual modeled ending
correspondence.finding: The last bend and actual ending lie within the mapped Pampa de las Salinas area. The salt-flat destination is supported, but neither original independently traces the selected internal continuation. The ending is not declared an ocean outlet, a surveyed river mouth or proof of permanent surface flow.

The chosen southwestern opening and its northeastward approach occupy the Imataca headward setting. The historical study associates Amacuro headwaters, La Horqueta and the mouth of Polvo de Oro with this upper drainage, but its point list is not proof that the whole selected opening follows one of those named channels. The thematic chapter map does not resolve this initial route separately from generalized drainage and boundary linework.

The latter part of the first fragment runs northeast to the model join before the short eastward corridor. San Victor is an independently recorded historical Amacuro landmark, but that association does not establish every intervening selected reach or the first inter-fragment join. No exact source point, falls position or channel-name transition is assigned.

The eastward segment and its small initial southward deflection remain without adequate continuous channel mapping. La Lancha appears in the historical study's survey table, but a named point cannot supply the missing through-link or settle which feeder is selected.

The selection turns north from the eastward connector and continues toward its eastern bend. The regional thematic map depicts a receiving river corridor in this setting but does not adequately resolve both selected joins or every middle through-link. Its territorial shading and boundary linework are not treated as independent river-channel observations.

The selected eastern elbow turns into the northwestward lower corridor. The historical text distinguishes the Haiowa tributary from Amacuro, and the chapter map shows the broad turning waterway. Neither source supplies enough unobscured detail to assign every joining arm at the selected bend or declare the complete fragment established. Haiowa is not used as an alternative name for the whole selected river.

Figure14 shows a northwestward waterway leading to the coastal opening west of the separately depicted Barima outlet. This is consistent with the chapter's distinct Amacuro and Barima prose. Portions of the lower waterway lie beneath thematic text and arrows, so the complete lower route and the final model join are not presented as continuously inspected channel evidence.

The chapter and independent historical geographical description identify coastal mangrove, swamp, tidal and floodplain environments in the region. Neither establishes each selected wetland through-link, a named lake or reservoir transit, modern tidal direction, present navigation conditions or uninterrupted surface flow. No selected lake/reservoir identity is asserted, and regional wetland context does not close the channel gaps.

The actual final tip lies at the small coastal opening reached by the northwestward waterway on Figure14, southwest of the separate Barima opening. That bounded terminal setting is visible at the regional map scale. It is not the endpoint of fragment11257, Mora Passage, Waini, a surveyed official river-mouth vertex or a claim about the current shoreline.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen eastern feeder and initial southwestern descent
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening is on the inland side of the eastern divide, north of Tiguana. Map 4.3 depicts the small southwestern feeder and its joins into the valley south of Mesa El Sauzal. The regional Cerro Prieto headwater description is not treated as the exact source of this selected feeder; its individual name remains unassigned.

The selected western turns follow the channel labeled San Gregorio between Mesa El Sauzal and Mesa Rosario in the integrated study. The neighboring San Juan and San Antonio approaches lie farther north and are not substituted for the selected upper route.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwestern bends and intermediate joins below Mesa Rosario
correspondence.finding: The selected southwestern descent, westward lowland bends and successive junctions correspond to the mapped network continuing into the Las Bramonas corridor. Both northward joining channels and the separate southern Batequito and La Picota routes were considered. The municipal map uses Las Bramonas at a broader upper-corridor scope; exact name-transition points and aliases are not inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: Central plain and southern loop east and south of Benito Juárez
correspondence.finding: The selected westward passage and pronounced southern loop match the connected channel north of Ciudad Constitución and south of Benito Juárez. The continuous return toward the lower Las Bramonas reach is visible in both thematic compilations. Agricultural-plain context is retained without asserting that each selected segment is a managed drain.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Las Bramonas corridor around Ramaditas
correspondence.finding: The northwestern turn and westward lower course match the repeatedly labeled Las Bramonas channel by Ramaditas. The source maps distinguish this route from neighboring coastal drainage and the more southerly San Luis system. The nearby El Ihuajil reservoir is on San Luis and is not a selected reservoir crossing.

correspondence.component_scope: Northward final turn and lagoon-side terminal near Puerto Adolfo López Mateos
correspondence.finding: The final northward bend reaches the inlet beside Puerto Adolfo López Mateos, followed by the selected short westward ending at the lagoon-side coastal margin. The integrated-study coastal enlargements and municipal relief map support this connection at ordinary estuarine scale. The ending is landward of Isla Magdalena; no passage across the barrier island to the open Pacific is asserted.
The supplied selection begins with an eastward headward reach and southern bend. No original source was read that establishes its river name, chosen branch or connection to the next selected reach.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern sweep and eastward upper corridor
correspondence.finding: The selected northern sweep and subsequent eastward upper corridor were considered from the supplied path only. Source support for each intervening connection, possible small waterbody and distinct reach name remains absent.

The selected eastward-to-southeastward continuation and its successive joining settings have no inspected independent cartographic support. Basin membership or catalogue titles do not establish these through-links.

The selected middle southward corridor, bends and downstream connections remain unsupported by original-source observations. The unavailable basin report and Pedro Canário map cannot be treated as evidence.
The selected lower eastward reaches have not been matched against usable original cartography. No wetland, reservoir, managed passage or alternative branch is assumed absent.

The selected southeastern approach toward the coast remains unverified. Neither the unavailable district map nor discovery references establish the chosen lower channel, any estuarine or wetland passage, or its continuation.

The supplied model labels the last reach as a sea terminal. No primary map or prose was read that verifies the actual final through-link and coastal outlet; the model endpoint is orientation only, not independent proof.
